items.title: OpenAI 宣布 AI 模型取得三项科学突破，涉及局部光滑猜想、指数时间假设与杨–米尔斯理论
items.description: OpenAI 于 10 月 27 日宣布其 AI 模型在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域取得三项研究突破。数学上给出了所有维度下局部光滑猜想的证明，从而解决挂谷猜想与斯坦因限制猜想；计算机科学上给出推翻指数时间假设（ETH）的证明，暗示相关计算任务可能有更快算法；物理学上提出量子色动力学及标准模型一种统一完备化的严格存在性证明，涉及杨–米尔斯千禧年难题的一部分。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/jxpzj0z4beg1r0cktwzc0tmwe

items.title: 红果短剧：网传“红果短剧年收入 400 亿”等为不实信息
items.description: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，红果短剧官方账号发布声明，否认了网络上流传的“年化收入逼近 400 亿元”“今年营收达 420 亿至 450 亿元”等说法。 红果短剧官方声明称，经核实上述收入数据不实，网传内容中标注的“机构数据”“行业数据”“专家预计”均非官方信息，据此展开的比较、推算和延伸解读也没有事实依据。 红果短剧同时表示，公司大部分收入持续用于内容创作者分账、版权保底和优质内容扶持。 这轮传闻的核心是将红果短剧的收入体量与中国电影市场全年总票房直接对比。 多个流传版本引用“年化收入逼近 400 亿元”的说法，与 2025 年中国电影全年 518.32 亿元的总票房并列，进而推导出短剧平台“碾压电影产业”的结论。IT之家查询发现，字节跳动官方从未正式披露过红果短剧的单独营收数据。 相关阅读： 《 红果短剧上线防沉迷提醒视频，正逐步覆盖更多用户 》 《 看视频赚钱福利没了，红果短剧计划年底下线金币功能 》

items.title: Anthropic 重申：我们永远不会在 Claude 对话中展示广告
items.description: IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，Anthropic 公司昨日向美国证券交易委员会提交 S-1 注册文件，计划首次公开发行 A 类普通股，并申请在纳斯达克以“ANT”为股票代码上市。 IT之家注意到，Anthropic 在 IPO 文件中重申： 公司永远不会在 Claude 的对话中展示广告 。 该公司还在文件中写道：“人们会向 Claude 托付最重要的工作，也会向它提问最私人的话题。 我们希望 ， Claude 的唯一目标是为用户提供有帮助的回答 。一旦广告成为企业收入目标的一部分，优化用户参与度的压力往往就会增加，我们选择不让这种压力进入 Claude。” 值得注意的是，Anthropic 曾批评竞争对手 OpenAI 在 ChatGPT 中投放广告，并警告称这种广告形式可能比传统广告更具操纵性。

items.title: 刚刚，GPT-6.1 Terra 骨折价发布，Agent 时代的打工模型来了
items.description: OpenAI 又卷起了大模型的性价比。 #欢迎关注爱范儿官方微信公众号：爱范儿（微信号：ifanr），更多精彩内容第一时间为您奉上。
items.author: 莫崇宇
items.content: 就在刚刚，OpenAI 正式发布新一代模型 GPT-6.1 Terra，主打更快的响应速度、更强的视觉理解和电脑操作能力，以及更低的使用成本。 相比上一代 GPT-5.6 Terra，新模型的标准 API 价格直接降低 50%，但在复杂任务执行、事实准确率和编程能力上均有明显提升。尤其是在部分专业任务测试中，GPT-6.1 Terra 已经能够接近旗舰模型 GPT-6 Astra 的表现，Token 价格却只有后者的十分之一。 OpenAI 将其定位为一款面向高频工作场景的高效模型，希望让更多企业和开发者能够以更低的成本，将 AI Agent 真正应用到日常工作中。 例如，用户可以让它根据建筑设计图纸创建 3D 模型，或者逐帧检查动画影片，为修复团队制作带有时间码的镜头记录。企业还可以利用它读取收到的发票，并将相关信息自动录入财务软件。 在衡量 AI Agent 完成专业工作能力的 Agents’ Last Exam 测试中，GPT-6.1 Terra 的表现相当突出。 更值得关注的是，同样在这一测试中，GPT-6.1 Terra 已经能够达到 GPT-6 Astra 的水平，而标准 API 的 Token 单价仅为后者的十分之一。

items.content: 现在，打开电视准备看部电影，首先映入眼帘的却是一段开机广告。好不容易进了主页，扑面而来的又是满屏的海报推荐、会员充值弹窗，中途按个暂停还会跳出一整张促销贴片。 上周，开发者 Gathin 在社交平台上发了一组给父母改电视的照片。按他的描述，家里的小米电视连打开 Netflix 前都要先看一段赞助广告。 于是，他把电视型号交给了编程助手 Claude Code，让它通过 Wi-Fi 接入设备，一口气停用了 25 个系统组件，再写一个极简桌面——原来杂乱的主页，一下子就变得清爽起来。 短短几天，项目迅速收获了约 1.37 万颗 Star， 「天下苦智能电视久矣」了属于是 。在 Reddit 的相关讨论区中，挤满了追问自家机型能否适配的用户，不少人也陆续贴出自己改造后的极简首页。 只要连上同一局域网、开启电视的调试权限，AI 就能顺着终端接口排查正在运行的几百个应用组件。哪些是开机广告，哪些是偷偷上报收视数据的遥测程序，AI 逐个筛查并下达命令将其「冻结」，最后再换上一个纯净的开源桌面。 另一位 YouTuber Ansub Khan 也记录了自己的改造过程，并将项目开源为 TV Detox 。在他原本的那台电视上，开机默认会自动播放嘈杂的轮播内容。

As the AI boom strains computing capacity, Nvidia has backed Indian startup Simplismart in a $14 million funding round, betting on software that helps companies run AI models more efficiently and, in some cases, with fewer GPUs. Nvidia participated in the all-primary Series B round alongside Accel, Shastra VC, and Micromax, with Dallas Venture Capital leading the investment. The deal values the four-year-old startup at about $100 million, including the new funding. Companies are nowadays spending heavily on GPUs to power AI applications, but running those models reliably and economically at scale remains a challenge. Different workloads demand distinct trade-offs between speed, cost, and performance. Deploying and operating AI models to meet business requirements often also requires complex adjustments. Simplismart says its software automates much of that work, tailoring how models run on existing computing infrastructure instead of requiring customers to manage those configurations themselves. “Nobody actually needs the fastest or the cheapest inference,” Amritanshu Jain (pictured above, left), co-founder and CEO of Simplismart, said in an interview. He added that companies instead need to run AI models at speeds and costs that make sense for their specific applications.

The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse. OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines. “There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.” The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. Once it is connected to your calendar, email, computer and other tools, the agent tries to help you get your work done.

SpaceX has reached a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data center equipment, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing Monday . In a statement, SpaceX called the deal the “largest committed GPU financing” . Under the agreement, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, the New York-based private equity giant, will buy the chips and related server hardware, then lease the equipment to SpaceX. The leases will last about five to five-and-a-quarter years, beginning when each tranche of equipment is delivered, according to the filing. SpaceX expects the deal to close by year-end, subject to closing conditions, with leases starting in the first half of 2027 as the GPUs and related equipment arrive. The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.

Three months after Elon Musk declared that Grok would release a full-length, “historically accurate” movie version of “The Odyssey,” Grok has published a whole seven minutes, which the company is now calling “Episode 1 of our Odyssey series.” Musk had previously lashed out at Christopher Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” because Nolan cast nonwhite and transgender actors. And Nolan is, in many ways, a perfect foil for Musk — while SpaceX and Tesla CEO hypes up data centers in space and posts an unending stream of AI-generated content, Nolan has described himself as “a techno-skeptic ” and said that before AI, he’d never seen a technology “so completely rejected by the public.” And while Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” certainly used plenty of visual effects, it’s primarily a feat of practical filmmaking , with a shoot spanning six countries and a cast and crew of thousands. After its release in July, the film became an extraordinary box office success , selling out Imax screenings for months and becoming the likely front-runner at the next Academy Awards . As for the Grok version of “The Odyssey” (created in collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker), well, you can watch for yourself.

items.description: "Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech."

AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch). Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity. “Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said. Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants? Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.”

Some of these AI wearables — including necklaces, rings, and wristbands, as well as portable devices — serve as productivity tools, while others claim to act as friendly companions listening to your everyday thoughts. Even OpenAI is working on a compact AI companion device. Bee is an affordable pendant priced at $49.99 that can either be clipped to your clothing or worn like a fitness band. This device records everything it hears and learns your routines and preferences to create reminders and notes for you. It even features a mute button for those times you want some privacy. items.title: Will AI expose the rickety infrastructure of the internet?
items.description: The moment you realize the internet is "held together by glue and dreams."
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. A startling announcement went out earlier this week: Due to recently discovered vulnerabilities in the open source programming language PHP, website owners had to immediately patch their sites — or if they couldn’t update right away, they should take the sites down to be safe. On this week’s episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the significance of the PHP-ocalypse and whether we’ll see more incidents like this in the future. Sean called this “a real reckoning moment” that highlights how “when you get down to the bone level of the internet,” everything seems to be “held together by glue and dreams.” And with widespread access to large language models and AI agents, it’s only going to become easier to find these vulnerabilities. (That said, these specific vulnerabilities were found by human researchers , not AI models.) Kirsten, meanwhile, wondered if we’re about to see the “next level of prepper doom […] because you could see how banks could get exploited, and [with] data and privacy concerns, it just feels a lot bigger than we can fix right now.”
